ratings_why.fun: Placing Lurkers beside cheap fodder or alone in gaps is a real board puzzle every turn, and a chain of Springs is a fight moment worth watching.
ratings_why.distinct: Hidden units in their own slots, woken by a death next to them, play unlike any of today's tribes; the Patient side is more familiar growth.

verdict_why: One small wording fix (Purse-Web Elder's 'it') and a trim of the Worshipful Master's text would finish it; the core reads well now.

points.text: Purse-Web Elder: 'it gains +1/+1' could mean the Elder or the Lurker. Say 'that Lurker gains +1/+1 permanently'.

The Worshipful Master's text is a paragraph of exceptions. Move 'Springs only when no other Lurker is under a Lid' into a short keyword-style line and put the summon placement in the rules, so the card reads in one glance.
The Lodge fantasy lives mostly in names; one card that plays the ballot box (say, a When played that blackballs a shop unit so it can't appear for you) would put the club into what the cards do.
Say on the card that the chain carries on (each new Spring wakes its own neighbours), since that is the payoff players need to see.

Wafer-Lid Sentry reads well now, but it is the longest non-capstone text; a shorter form like 'Twice a fight: when an enemy attacks a unit next to your Lurker, that Lurker Springs at it first' would keep the rest in the rules.

standouts.why: Heath Wolf Mother is the tribe in one line: hidden, knocked, comes up carrying her young, and the young are the next knocks.
Signora Corkhinge's lid that closes again is the fantasy and a clear, strong rule in one sentence.
Tapwell grows whichever way you play him, so a new player learns both Patient and Spring from one Tier 1 card.

weakest.why: Ballooning Money Spider is a plain deathrattle body; nothing about gossamer or luck shows in play.
The Worshipful Master's payoff is great but the card takes a paragraph to read, which is hard at shop speed.
Grit-Dresser is a generic lowest-Attack buffer with little of the Lodge in it.

flags.note: Repeating every Spring effect with Diadem and Corkhinge can be a very large fight; the designer marked it as the high roll on purpose.
An all-Lurker board Springs everything at Start of Combat, and with the Orbweaver that is a burst of double-damage Cleave hits before the enemy acts.
